task.name: review-semantic refuses a first evaluation until the operator asserts an empty baseline by flag
task.story_text:
## Observed

Running `forge review-semantic 433` by hand on an hdp feature issue with no prior evaluation refuses with:

```
[review-semantic] semantic baseline required before revealing evaluator output for issue-433 (8005929e…). Freeze it with --freeze-empty-baseline or --baseline-defect-id DEFECT_ID.
```

The automatic path, which landed on release/v0.16 as #2966 and is not in rc17, the runtime this was observed on, does not have this step: per `docs/reference/semantic-readiness.md`, sprint admission evaluates a policy-required issue itself and freezes an empty baseline marked `automatic` when none exists. Only the manual command demands the assertion. The operator reached the manual command because `forge status --ready` reported the issue `BLOCKED:semantic_review_not_ratified` and nothing in that output said the evaluation would run on its own at sprint entry, so the natural reading was "go run the review."

## Expected

The manual command and the automatic path treat an absent baseline the same way on a first evaluation: it is the empty baseline, recorded as such, with the flag remaining for the operator who wants to pin a specific defect. A readiness listing that withholds an issue for a missing evaluation says the evaluation runs at sprint admission, so an operator is not sent to a hand-run command the system would have performed anyway.

## Impact

An operator who checks readiness before spending, which is the advised discipline, is routed into a refusal-and-retry cycle per issue that the automatic path never incurs, and concludes the gate is more manual than it is.


## Diagnosis

**Baseline:** `a7297712813cb7d054269f0399881ba451864e13` captured at `2026-09-12T00:45:36.367541+00:00`

**Inspected files:**

- `src/theforge/cli/eval_cmd.py` — `sha256:901b77692c751e71e723386c18cdee7922e10c59b5d720b2b7486063f87d9397`
- `src/theforge/eval/semantic_runner.py` — `sha256:df4d187bd7cdc19c4db280b7e64d654f9824330d23f42253cdb3a1951faccc77`
- `src/theforge/eval/semantic_auto.py` — `sha256:21e6c8ffac4c57c181aabd949ab5a9d08171191254d1afb7e7e7a8520c0f413b`
- `docs/reference/semantic-readiness.md` — `sha256:bbaa636d771122f15720ee4c6d33e449a33f1cdaa64f4ae12e65dcda17ac23cb`
- `docs/guides/cli-reference.md` — `sha256:e64b4ad32bb00ad75db361423a3766426a659cf602921e49cf1ad58f0b69d578`
- `tests/test_cli_semantic_eval.py` — `sha256:2438da7887258c6a1f01d8e2ae745a292f1d9c426ab5adae618b5380d2c2e835`

### Observed symptom

`forge review-semantic ISSUE` refuses to run a first-ever evaluation of an
issue that has no frozen semantic baseline yet, printing:
"[review-semantic] semantic baseline required before revealing evaluator
output for issue-N (<digest>). Freeze it with --freeze-empty-baseline or
--baseline-defect-id DEFECT_ID." and exiting 1. The automatic evaluation that
runs at sprint admission (`ensure_semantic_evaluation`, shipped as #2966)
never hits this refusal: when it finds no baseline for the revision it
invokes the same evaluator with an empty baseline supplied automatically.
The two callers of the same underlying function therefore behave differently
for the identical "no baseline yet" case.

### Reproduction / evidence

Source inspection at HEAD (release/v0.16):
- src/theforge/cli/eval_cmd.py:253-262 (`cmd_review_semantic`): builds
  `baseline_input` as `None` unless the operator passed
  `--freeze-empty-baseline` or `--baseline-defect-id`. `None` is then passed
  as `baseline_defect_ids` to `review_issue_semantically`.
- src/theforge/eval/semantic_runner.py:280-288 (`review_issue_semantically`):
  when `semantic_store.frozen_baseline(...)` is `None` (no baseline exists)
  and `baseline_defect_ids is None`, it raises
  `SemanticBaselineRequiredError` — exactly the message the operator
  reported for issue #433.
- src/theforge/cli/eval_cmd.py:273-279: catches that exception and prints
  the "Freeze it with --freeze-empty-baseline or --baseline-defect-id
  DEFECT_ID" refusal message reported in the issue.
- src/theforge/eval/semantic_auto.py:405-429 (`ensure_semantic_evaluation`,
  the automatic sprint-admission path): before calling
  `review_issue_semantically`, it explicitly checks
  `semantic_store.frozen_baseline(readiness.input_digest) is None` and, if
  so, sets `baseline_defect_ids = ()` (an empty tuple, not `None`) so the
  call never raises `SemanticBaselineRequiredError` — it freezes an empty
  baseline with `BASELINE_PROVENANCE_AUTOMATIC` and proceeds straight to
  evaluation.
This is a direct, first-order comparison of the two call sites against the
same shared function, not a re-run of the operator's manual repro (gh CLI
access to issue #433 was not exercised in this investigation).

### Hypotheses tested

- **[confirmed]** cmd_review_semantic omits the same 'treat no-baseline as empty-baseline' default that the automatic admission path applies, so the CLI alone still requires an explicit flag.
  - Evidence: eval_cmd.py:255-262 computes baseline_input=None when neither --freeze-empty-baseline nor --baseline-defect-id is passed, which review_issue_semantically treats as 'no assertion' and raises SemanticBaselineRequiredError. semantic_auto.py:405-413 performs the equivalent check itself (frozen_baseline(...) is None) and substitutes baseline_defect_ids=() instead of leaving it None before calling the identical function, so its call never raises.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Directly read eval_cmd.py, semantic_runner.py, and semantic_auto.py at HEAD; not a restatement of the issue report or any prior diagnosis.
- **[ruled out]** The refusal is caused by a genuine safety invariant in SemanticReviewStore.freeze_baseline that also blocks the automatic path, so both paths are equally restrictive and the reported asymmetry does not exist.
  - Evidence: semantic_auto.py explicitly special-cases the missing-baseline condition and pre-supplies () before calling review_issue_semantically, specifically to avoid re-hitting the same guard cmd_review_semantic leaves untouched. The store itself has no additional gate beyond what review_issue_semantically already applies uniformly to both callers.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Directly observed in source; the module's own docstring (semantic_auto.py:1-31) independently restates the same design intent, which is a prior assertion about intended behavior but the code-level asymmetry was verified independently of that docstring.

### Confirmed cause

`cmd_review_semantic` (src/theforge/cli/eval_cmd.py) does not apply the same
"absent baseline == empty baseline" default that the automatic
sprint-admission path (`ensure_semantic_evaluation` in
src/theforge/eval/semantic_auto.py) applies before calling the shared
`review_issue_semantically`. When the operator supplies neither
`--freeze-empty-baseline` nor `--baseline-defect-id`, the CLI passes
`baseline_defect_ids=None` through to `review_issue_semantically`, which
interprets `None` as "no baseline assertion was made" and raises
`SemanticBaselineRequiredError` on a first evaluation. The automatic path
instead detects the same "no baseline exists" condition and substitutes an
empty tuple `()` before calling the identical function, so it freezes an
empty baseline (provenance `automatic`) and proceeds without ever raising.
The two callers of one shared function diverge only in this
None-vs-empty-tuple default, producing the reported asymmetry.

Support: eval_cmd.py:255-262 sets baseline_input to None unless a flag is given;
semantic_runner.py:283-288 raises SemanticBaselineRequiredError exactly when
baseline is None and baseline_defect_ids is None; semantic_auto.py:405-413
performs the equivalent "no baseline yet" check and passes () instead of
leaving the argument None, then calls the same review_issue_semantically at
semantic_auto.py:417-429. This is a first-hand structural comparison, not a
restatement of any existing bug report or commit message.
Support provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. All three files were read directly in this investigation; no prior diagnosis or commit message was consulted for the mechanism, only for the surrounding docs (semantic-readiness.md, cli-reference.md) used to confirm documented intent matched code.

### Affected code path

src/theforge/cli/eval_cmd.py:253-279 (cmd_review_semantic baseline_input
computation and SemanticBaselineRequiredError handling); contrast with
src/theforge/eval/semantic_auto.py:405-429 (ensure_semantic_evaluation's
empty-baseline default) and the shared
src/theforge/eval/semantic_runner.py:280-303 (review_issue_semantically
baseline branch).

### Fix-success criterion

Running `forge review-semantic ISSUE` by hand on an issue with no prior
semantic baseline succeeds on the first invocation without any
--freeze-empty-baseline or --baseline-defect-id flag, freezing an empty
baseline (recorded with an appropriate provenance, e.g. human/manual) and
revealing the evaluator's findings — matching what the automatic
sprint-admission path already does for the same "no baseline yet"
condition. --baseline-defect-id must remain available and effective for an
operator who wants to pin specific defect ids into the baseline instead of
an empty one on that first evaluation. A subsequent invocation against an
already-frozen baseline must not silently refreeze it.

### Related findings (out of scope)

> These are adjacent problems noticed during investigation. They are **not** the cause of this issue's symptom and are **out of scope for this fix** — triage them separately under the linked issue. Do not implement them as part of this issue.

- forge status --ready's BLOCKED:semantic_review_not_ratified reason code does not indicate that sprint admission will run the missing evaluation automatically, which is what sent the operator to the manual command in the first place.

### Advisory repair proposal

> Advisory only: this is an unverified repair idea from the investigation, not part of the confirmed diagnosis contract.

Mirror semantic_auto.py's pattern in cmd_review_semantic: when
baseline_ids is empty and freeze_empty is False, check whether a baseline
already exists for the digest; if none exists, default baseline_input to
() rather than None (instead of relying on --freeze-empty-baseline to
produce that same value). This would let --freeze-empty-baseline become a
no-op/deprecated flag rather than a required gesture, while
--baseline-defect-id still works for pinning specific ids. Not verified
against the full test suite (test_cli_semantic_eval.py) for side effects on
the "baseline already exists + new defect ids supplied" refreeze branch.

### Notes

This investigation did not exercise `gh issue view 433` or the actual CLI
invocation end-to-end (no network/gh access attempted); the confirmed cause
rests on direct source comparison of the two call sites against the shared
function, which is sufficient to explain the exact error string reported in
the issue. The issue's "Expected" section also raises a second, narrower
concern — that `forge status --ready`'s BLOCKED:semantic_review_not_ratified
message does not tell the operator that admission will run the evaluation
itself — which is a documentation/messaging gap distinct from the
review-semantic refusal mechanism and is recorded separately below rather
than folded into this fix.
